title: Pilot- and lab-scale spray-drying conditions and protein content of legume-grass concentrates
citation: Echeverria-Jaramillo, E., Jørgensen, A. K., Jørgensen, M. K., Gregersen Echers, S., Lübeck, M., & Orlien, V. (2026). source_locations: Materials and Methods, LGC Production and spray-drying conditions

geography: Three commercial legume-grass fields in Jutland, Denmark
license: CC BY, as stated by the University of Copenhagen research portal record for the final published version.
material_scope: Accumulated mixture of RuBisCO-rich legume-grass concentrates produced from commercial blends of red and/or white clover and ryegrass, with other grasses in one field. The study's LGC was produced by pilot-scale screw pressing and membrane filtration; the drying comparison used pilot- and laboratory-scale equipment. This is not the GreenHub isoelectric precipitate or a roadside-grass product.
experimental_conditions: Leaves were harvested 2023-09-05 through 2023-10-19 from three fields in Jutland. The pilot condition used a Niro Atomiser Mobile Minor spray dryer at 220–240 °C inlet and 68–70 °C outlet air temperature. The laboratory condition used a Yamato Ohkawara DL41 at 246 °C inlet and 83–85 °C outlet air temperature. Table 2 reports crude protein of the resulting powders on a dry basis with reported uncertainty.
data_scope: Two source-linked observations pair the two dryer-scale conditions with Table 2 crude-protein means and reported uncertainty. Temperature setpoints are preserved as ranges where the source reports ranges. The raw-data table does not provide feed solids, feed flow, atomizer settings, drying-air flow, energy use, evaporation rate, powder recovery, or powder moisture; these fields remain blank.
limitations: Reference-only; no GreenHub parameter, default, cost, energy equation, or runtime result is activated.
Feedstock is a cultivated Danish mixed legume-grass concentrate from membrane filtration, not a roadside-grass isoelectric curd or GreenHub protein product.
The experiment compares two equipment scales and different operating conditions, so scale effects cannot be separated from temperature and equipment effects.

No feed solids, feed rate, drying-air flow, atomization settings, thermal duty, electrical demand, powder recovery, final moisture, or closed drying mass balance are reported in this extract; do not infer these values.

The article text and Table 2 disagree on the reported uncertainty for LGT2 D[4,3] particle size (24.08 ± 0.17 versus 24.08 ± 0.31 µm). Particle size is deliberately excluded pending source clarification.
The authors state that data can be made available on request; raw replicate data are not publicly included in the article.
conversion_or_processing: Two operating cases and Table 2 dry-basis protein means/uncertainties were transcribed as reported. No unit conversion, averaging, regression, drying energy calculation, moisture inference, or particle-size transcription was performed.
uncertainty: Table 2 provides reported protein mean ± uncertainty. The accessible article text does not establish whether this is SD, SE, or a confidence interval; the CSV preserves the magnitude but explicitly marks its statistical type as unspecified.
